```text
SOURCE: "Are We Ready For An Agent-Native Memory System?" Wei Zhou, Xuanhe Zhou (corresponding author), Shaokun Han, Hongming Xu, Guoliang Li, Zhiyu Li, Feiyu Xiong, Fan Wu (Shanghai Jiao Tong, Tsinghua, MemTensor). arXiv:2606.24775v1, 23 Jun 2026. Preprint.
Path: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/03-agentic-foundations/sources/zhou-2026-we-ready-agent-native-memory.pdf

COVERAGE: 14 of 14 pages, 91,599 of 91,599 chars. Pages 1-13 are body text and the references begin on p.13-14. I read the references only up to [32] and skimmed the rest for origins. There is no appendix. The paper has no limitations section, and the "promising directions" its abstract promises do not appear in the text. I did not read the target note beyond its front matter and first paragraphs.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: No single memory architecture dominates across workloads. Effectiveness depends on matching the memory structure to the workload bottleneck.
  number: none (12 systems, 2 baselines, 5 workloads, 11 datasets)
  setup: 12 systems (MemoChat, Mem0, MEM1, MemAgent, MemTree, Zep, Mem0g, Cognee, LightMem, SimpleMem, MemOS, MemoryOS, A-MEM, Letta) plus Long Context and Embedding RAG baselines. Benchmarks are LoCoMo, LongMemEval (via MemoryAgentBench), DB-Bench (LifelongAgentBench), LongBench. Several backbones are used, including GPT-5.4 variants.
  quote: "No single memory architecture dominates all scenarios. Composite hybrid systems lead on conversational QA, while graph-based methods excel in single-hop factual recall but struggle with temporal reasoning."
  where: p.2 (Finding 1, O1 on p.7-8)
- claim: Leaders differ by workload. Zep leads LongMemEval LLM-judge accuracy, MemOS leads LoCoMo exact match, and on DB-Bench the best exact match and task success go to Long Context and MemoChat.
  number: Zep 48.0 judge accuracy; Cognee 35.3 ROUGE-L F1; MemOS 11.5 EM; Long Context 48.20 EM; MemoChat 55.40 task success
  setup: Figure 7, default backbone. Per-system numbers are from the figure.
  quote: "Zep reaches 48.0 LLM Judge Accuracy and Cognee attains 35.3 ROUGE-L F1; (2) Hybrid filtering is strongest on LoCoMo exactness, where MemOS reaches 11.5 Exact Match (EM); and (3) Trace-preserving memories remain strongest on DB-Bench, where Long Context achieves 48.20 EM and MemoChat reaches 55.40 Task Success Rate."
  where: p.7
- claim: Letta (MemGPT) is not strong in this testbed on conversational memory. It scores 0.0 EM on LoCoMo and 0.0 on the Table 2 temporal slice.
  number: LoCoMo EM 0.0, Answer F1 5.3 (Figure 7); LongMemEval ROUGE-L F1 7.8; LongMemEval judge accuracy 23.0
  setup: Fig 7 and Table 2. This matters for the MemGPT-centred note.
  quote: "Letta (MemGPT)0.0 7.1 17.8 5.7 12.0 8.8"
  where: p.9 (Table 2); Figure 7 values on p.8
- claim: Letta scores 61.6 on DB-Bench. This is the highest score in the figure, above the text's stated leaders, and the text does not discuss it.
  number: 61.6 EM and 61.6 task success
  setup: Figure 7(g,h) data labels. The text names Long Context (48.20) as best EM and MemoChat (55.40) as best task success, which conflicts with the figure labels.
  quote: "Letta\n61.6" (Figure 7g and 7h extraction labels, "(g) DB-Bench: EM")
  where: p.8. Treat as an internal inconsistency to verify against the figure image.
- claim: Retrieval is an evidence-completion problem, not a top-1 ranking problem. Structured memory holds up as evidence gets farther from the query. Flat Embedding RAG collapses.
  number: Recall@1: SimpleMem 39.0. A-MEM 69.5 / 85.9 and MemTree 59.7 / 80.5 at Recall@5 / @10.
  setup: LoCoMo, 8 systems, hit means the gold evidence appears in top-k source-id groups. Recall@10 is binned by session distance (1-5 to 26-31).
  quote: "SimpleMem achieves the highest Recall@1 (39.0), but A-MEM and MemTree become clearly stronger at larger retrieval budgets, reaching 69.5/85.9 and 59.7/80.5 on Recall@5/@10, respectively"
  where: p.9
- claim: Graph-based memory handles knowledge updates best. Plain Long Context and Embedding RAG are weakest at separating stale from updated facts. The abstract's "hallucinations of the past" refers to systems that lack lifecycle management.
  number: Zep 44.4 Substring EM and 36.8 ROUGE-L F1 on Knowledge Update; Cognee 18.7 / 35.8 on Temporal Reasoning
  setup: Table 2, LongMemEval Knowledge Update and Temporal Reasoning slices and the LoCoMo temporal slice. 11 systems.
  quote: "Zep leads Knowledge Update with 44.4 Substring EM and 36.8 ROUGE-L F1; (2) Relationally organized retrieval is strongest on temporally dispersed evidence, where Cognee leads Temporal Reasoning with 18.7 Substring EM and 35.8 ROUGE-L F1"
  where: p.9
- claim: Backbone choice changes absolute scores more than it changes which memory pipeline works. Stronger LLMs help answer wording only after the evidence has been located.
  number: MemOS Answer F1 of 32.2, 41.2, 38.6 and 41.2 across the 4 backbones
  setup: LoCoMo, 6 memory settings, 4 backbones (Qwen3-B, DeepSeek-Chat, GPT-5.4-mini, GPT-5.4; the extraction is garbled, so the names are read from the legend and are uncertain). A-MEM overtakes MemTree under GPT-5.4-mini and GPT-5.4.
  quote: "MemOS remains the strongest memory-based configuration at 32.2, 41.2, 38.6, and 41.2"
  where: p.9
- claim: At long horizons, structure-preserving memory beats long-context prompting and flat dense retrieval.
  number: SimpleMem 35.2 to 34.9 Short to Medium; Long Context 42.6 to 19.0; Embedding RAG 37.1 to 7.4 Answer F1
  setup: LongBench accuracy by length bucket, and LoCoMo Answer F1 as the evidence gap widens. Raw numbers are in the text; the figure is Fig 10.
  quote: "SimpleMem stays nearly unchanged from the Short to Medium buckets (35.2 to 34.9 Accuracy), whereas Long Context drops from 42.6 to 19.0"
  where: p.10
- claim: Cost is governed by maintenance scope, not by structure alone. Localized update paths are cost-efficient. Graph-wide consolidation and repeated whole-memory rewriting are the most expensive.
  number: LightMem 48.3 utility at 3.67 s; MemTree 63.5 at 15.9 s; MemoryOS 82.0 at 28.6 s; Cognee and Zep over 84 only after 116.5 s and 155.1 s. LongBench latency per query: Mem0 374.2, MemoChat 460.2, MemoryOS 490.0, A-MEM 552.1 s.
  setup: RQ5, 8 systems. Latency is construction time plus query time, per query. Utility is the mean of 6 min-max normalised metrics, so it is relative to this set of systems only.
  quote: "MemoryOS reaches 82.0 Normalized Utility only at 28.6 s, while Cognee and Zep exceed 84 utility only after 116.5 s and 155.1 s"
  where: p.10-11
- claim: Keeping the original text beats summarising or compressing it. A deeper tree only helps access and cannot restore dropped content.
  number: LightMem Raw 24.2 EM / 38.9 F1 on LoCoMo; Summary 8.5 / 15.6; Compressed holds on LoCoMo at 23.6 / 38.6 but LongMemEval Substring EM falls 26.0 to 10.7
  setup: Table 3 ablation: LightMem User-Only Raw, Summary and Compressed; MemTree flat vs deeper; Mem0 default vs graph store.
  quote: "User-Only Compressed remains close on LoCoMo (Ans. F1: 38.6 vs. 38.9; EM: 23.6 vs. 24.2) but drops sharply on LongMemEval (Substring EM: 10.7 vs. 26.0)"
  where: p.11
- claim: Heavier LLM extraction at write time can hurt downstream reasoning (the "late filtering principle"). Store broadly, filter late.
  number: MemOS Fast Memorize vs Fine Memorize on LoCoMo: 25.5 vs 2.5 EM, 40.8 vs 5.0 F1
  setup: Table 4. Fine Memorize is slightly better on LongMemEval (22.3 vs 20.7 Substr. EM; 30.2 vs 26.1 ROUGE-L). Also MemoChat heuristic vs LLM topic segmentation, and LightMem user-only vs user+assistant raw.
  quote: "MemOS Fast Memorize far exceeds Fine Memorize on LoCoMo (25.5 vs. 2.5 EM; 40.8 vs. 5.0 Ans. F1) despite lower LongMemEval scores (20.7 vs. 22.3 Substr. EM; 26.1 vs. 30.2 ROUGE-L F1)"
  where: p.12
- claim: Explicit lightweight query planning and balanced dense-sparse fusion improve retrieval. Adding a reflection step on top of planning does not.
  number: SimpleMem Planning Only 20.7 Ans. F1 / 90.6 recall vs No Planning 18.7 / 86.4; A-MEM Hybrid-Balanced 24.6 vs Sparse-Leaning 23.0
  setup: Table 5, LoCoMo and LongMemEval.
  quote: "SimpleMem achieves its best performance with Planning Only, reaching 20.7 Ans. F1, 90.6 Strict Rec., 21.7 Substr. EM, and 27.9 ROUGE-L F1, above both No Planning and Planning + Reflect."
  where: p.12
- claim: Conservative consolidation is the best default maintenance policy. Delayed flushing and forced single-topic summaries both lose accuracy. The gains from conservative merging are small.
  number: MemoryOS default 23.2 F1 / 22.4 Substr. EM; Conservative-Merge 23.5 / 22.8; Delayed-Flush 20.6 / 19.5; MemoChat Topic1 16.2 / 16.8 vs default 16.6 / 18.4; Long Context 23.7 Substr. EM
  setup: Figure 12, LoCoMo only. The 0.3-0.4 difference for conservative merging has no variance reported.
  quote: "improves over default MemoryOS from 23.2 to 23.5 in Ans. F1 and from 22.4 to 22.8 in Substr. EM, whereas delaying flushes lowers the same system to 20.6/19.5"
  where: p.12-13
- claim: Agent memory is a stateful data-management system defined as a four-module tuple, distinct from RAG and from context engineering.
  number: none
  setup: Definitional framework, Section 2. RAG is "stateless, read-only retrieval". Context engineering curates the window each turn. Memory governs the persistent lifecycle.
  quote: "M_sys = ⟨R,S,Q,U⟩" (R = representation/storage, S = extraction, Q = retrieval/routing, U = maintenance)
  where: p.3

LIMITS
- No limitations section and no stated caveats. The conclusion says the testbed "will" be released, while the abstract links code.
- Single runs. No variance, confidence intervals or seeds are reported. Many ablation gaps are tiny (23.2 vs 23.5).
- Most numbers are lexical or LLM-judge metrics on LoCoMo, LongMemEval, DB-Bench and LongBench. Absolute scores are low (for example EM around 3 to 11 on LoCoMo).
- Some systems are absent from some benchmarks. Mem0g, MEM1 and Letta are missing from some panels. Several RQs use only 8 to 11 systems.
- Ablations vary one or two knobs per system (Tables 3 to 5), so "best default" claims are system-specific.
- Possible internal inconsistency on DB-Bench (Letta 61.6 in the figure vs the text naming Long Context and MemoChat as best).
- Authors MemTensor and Li/Xiong are affiliated with MemOS, one of the evaluated systems.
- The cost normalisation is relative within the evaluated set. Latency depends on the implementation and backbone.
- Dated: the arXiv ID is 2606.xxxxx (June 2026) and uses GPT-5.4. The Zep, MemOS and LightMem versions evaluated are not stated.

BUILDS ON
MemGPT (Packer et al. 2023, [25], called Letta); Mem0/Mem0g (Chhikara et al. 2025); Zep (Rasmussen et al. 2025); A-MEM; MemoChat (Lu et al. 2023); MemTree (Rezazadeh et al. 2025); LightMem (Fang et al. 2025); SimpleMem (Liu et al. 2026); MemOS (Li et al. 2025); MemoryOS (Kang et al. 2025); Cognee (Markovic et al. 2025); MemoRAG (as cited in the text). Benchmarks: LoCoMo (Maharana et al. 2024), LongMemEval (Wu et al. 2024), MemoryAgentBench (2026), LifelongAgentBench, LongBench (Bai et al. 2024). Framing: Anthropic "Effective context engineering" (2025); Hu et al. "Memory in the Age of AI Agents" (2025, arXiv:2512.13564); database-community evaluation [32].

CODE
None in the paper. The code is linked at https://github.com/OpenDataBox/MemoryData and the taxonomy at https://github.com/OpenDataBox/awesome-agent-memory.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.2): execution workflows of four memory designs (stream-and-reflection, hierarchical tiers like MemGPT, knowledge graph, composite hybrid). It shows MemGPT's core / recall / archival tiers with core_memory_append, core_memory_replace and archival_memory_insert / archival_memory_search function calls.
- Table 1 (p.4): taxonomy mapping each system to its representation, storage, extraction, retrieval and maintenance choices. Letta is marked as a "Context Tiers" composite on a relational DB, with function-calling retrieval and queue-flush eviction.
- Fig 6 (p.7): maintenance methods (versioning, eviction, consolidation, parametric).
- Fig 7 (p.8): per-system bar charts across LoCoMo, LongMemEval and DB-Bench.
- Fig 8 (p.8): Recall@k and the evidence-distance curve.
- Fig 10 (p.10): long-horizon degradation.
- Fig 11 (p.11): cost-utility frontier.
- The caption command was not run; the captions above come from the text extraction.

PROBLEMS
- The Fig 9 and Fig 12 axis labels are garbled in the extraction (font-encoding noise), so the backbone names are uncertain. The data in Fig 12 is partly given only in the text.
- Figure bar values come from extracted data labels, so Figure 7 may be misaligned. In particular, DB-Bench Letta 61.6 conflicts with the prose.
- No embedded instructions were found in the PDF.
- A tool-result preview of a different tool's instructions appeared in my first output. It was unrelated to the PDF and I ignored it.
```
